title: Characterization of tree-size languages
statement: For a size bound $T : \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{N}$ and a language $L$ over Boolean words, $L$ belongs to the class of languages of tree size at most $T$ if and only if there is a family of Boolean circuit trees, one on $n$ variables for each $n$, such that each tree has size at most $T(n)$ and, for every Boolean word $w$, membership of $w$ in $L$ is equivalent to the tree on $|w|$ variables evaluating to true on the assignment given by the entries of $w$.
hypotheses_covered: $T$ is a function from natural numbers to natural numbers
$L$ is a language over Boolean words
